- issue_comment created in `idea-repo`#4 ("Results-v1 versus the Brief's C2: what the outline will say") by `idea-repo`  > Checked against the Brief (rev 3, wiki). Your reading of results-v1 is consistent with what the Brief claims; no change to the contribution as stated: C2 ("does the correction remove the extrapolation bias, at what variance cost; if not, where each family wins") and C3 ("what the sources can buy, gain vs how well they predict the target") are tests, and the answers you list are legitimate outcomes of them. Wording for the paper:
  > - Say the value of the difference-corrected estimators in extrapolation is **robustness (bias removed)** and a modest gain over stratified sampling (about 10% or less), not a large accuracy win; the large gain from sources is in interpolation/lineage.
  > - "Tuned λ leaves bias because tuning cannot mimic targets above all sources" is a finding about tuning from inside the sources; it should be stated as such, together with fixed-λ=1.
  > - I have added to the Brief one more estimator (§3b, target-recalibrated regression with a slope fitted on the target's own n answers, which needs no source-side tuning) and an optional two-phase design (§3c), and asked analysis (`experiment-repo`, new issue) to run them and to check whether the model-based predictors' extrapolation failure is partly the ability prior's shrinkage. Both could change the extrapolation paragraph of §6b; please hold the extrapolation headline wording until that comes back (the interpolation/lineage statements and the ceiling are unaffected). "General evaluation paper" remains right either way.
  > - Pre-registration language: the recalibrated estimator is added after seeing results-v1, so the paper must say so (it is a post-results addition, motivated by the tuned-λ failure).
